title: throughput-heuristics-lab-odd-notes-dec03-2026
content:
Dec 03 2026 - Throughput heuristics lab - odd notes

Attendees: Imani (host), Carlos, Ava, Liam, Ravi + SRE on call (Maya)
Duration: 45m
Purpose: sync on the weird throughput drop observed in shadow-run-2026-11-30; capture quick experiments, hypotheses, and concrete next steps.

TL;DR
- Observed: 12–18% throughput drop on medium-seq (256) mixed-qa workload after kernel rollout + new batching heuristic. Latency p50 stable, p95 inflated ~40–80ms.
- Short repro: lab cluster r-3b, 4xA100s, kernel v2.14, batch heuristic = adaptive-window-v3.
- Immediate mitigation: pin serving nodes used in production to kernel v2.12 and batching default (window-v2) until can validate.

Run summary (quick):
- run A (control): kernel v2.12 + window-v2; sustained qps 3600, p95 230ms.
- run B (candidate): kernel v2.14 + window-v3; sustained qps 3100, p95 305ms.
- run C (candidate + kv-prime): v2.14 + window-v3 + aggressive-kv-prime (prewarm keys 40%); qps 3350, p95 270ms.
- run D (v2.14 + window-v3 + reduced-concurrency): qps 3380, p95 265ms (better but still below control).

Observations / oddities:
- Throughput drop correlates strongly with higher batch variance (we see more tiny batches + some very large batches) after adaptive-window-v3 enabled. Hypothesis: adaptive window expansion is mis-triggering during background KV-cache maintenance spikes.
- Flamegraphs show a new hot path in rpc-sender: extra copy on cuda buffer when batch size > 256 and sequence length variance > 0.5. This path wasn't present in v2.12.
- KV priming helped but not fully: suggests two separate factors (batch selection + cuda copy).
- Shadow traces (trace ids in linked artifacts) show spike windows aligned with autoscaler pod restarts in same AZ — surprising coupling with scheduling.

Diagnostics captured (where to find):
- perf traces: gs://redwood-perf/shadow/2026-11-30/trace-batch-xyz.json
- flamegraphs: gs://redwood-perf/flame/v2.14/batches-nov30.svg
- bench logs: /var/log/bench/throughput-lab/dec03-heatmap.log (on lab-host-07)
- k8s events: JIRA-RT-987 comments

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) adaptive-window-v3 logic expands window incorrectly when kv-cache cleanup frequency increases, creating batch variance that trips new cuda-copy path => throughput drop.
2) kernel v2.14 introduced a memcpy-at-edge optimization that regresses for mixed sequences when combined with autoshard placement.
3) AZ-level autoscaler flapping causes temporary churn in worker pools, increasing cold-starts + slow priming and amplifying the above (secondary).

Quick tests proposed (short):
- T1: run v2.14 + window-v3 but force window upper bound = 256 (cheap change) to see if limiting expansion avoids tiny/huge mix. Owner: Carlos. ETA: 12/05.
- T2: instrument rpc-sender memcpy count and attach sample traces to PR 673. Owner: Ava. ETA: 12/04.
- T3: full shadow with v2.12 kernel but window-v3 heuristic to isolate kernel vs heuristic. Owner: Liam. ETA: 12/06.
- T4: synthetic workload that simulates autoscaler-induced pod churn to measure amplification. Owner: Ravi + SRE Maya. ETA: 12/07.

Action items (concrete):
- [IMANI] open emergency config pin in prod for kernel -> v2.12 and batching heuristic -> window-v2 (done, see CONFLUENCE-1234).
- [CARLOS] prepare T1 patch and smoke-run on lab cluster. Link PR in JIRA-RT-987. (in progress)
- [AVA] add memcpy instrumentation + add guard logging for large-batch-copy path. Post observations to PR 673. (eta 12/04)
- [LIAM] run isolation shadow (v2.12 + window-v3). Collect qps and batch size histogram. (eta 12/06)
- [RAVI/SRE] run churn experiment and produce amplification factor report. (eta 12/07)
- [MAYA] check autoscaler logs for AZ flapping events 11/29-12/03 and correlate to node restarts. (eta 12/05)

Notes to self / stray items:
- There was a broken metric in the runner that undercounts small-batch events (fixed in local branch but not yet in lab) — may have masked earlier signal.
- Consider adding a small randomized delay jitter in batch-collector to avoid pathological alignment. Cheap experiment.
- Need to review the quantization path: kernel v2.14 introduced a new int8 fallback for attention kernels; double-check if copy path is related.

Decisions (for now):
- Rollback kernel in prod to v2.12 until T1/T2 validate.
- Keep adaptive-window-v3 disabled by default in production flags.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did kv-priming partially recover but not fully? Is priming timing mismatched with batch formation?
- Exact combination of sequence-length distribution that triggers memcpy path (need histogram join).
- Are there customer-facing latency regressions? quick check: gating dashboards show a small bump in some enterprise tenants (see CONFLUENCE-1234 notes).

Meeting end: 12:12pm. Next sync: ad-hoc after T1 results or weekly perf sync if not resolved (tentatively 12/08).

References / links (copy these into JIRA / PR):
- shadow-run logs: gs://redwood-perf/shadow/2026-11-30/
- PR with candidate kernel: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/673
- conf note: CONFLUENCE-1234 (prod rollback & incident notes)
- jira ticket: JIRA-RT-987 (throughput drop investigation)

Quick backlog ideas (not for immediate):
- rework batch selection to prefer stable window progression vs aggressive expansion; evaluate via A/B.
- explore move to zero-copy for rpc-sender path on large-batches only.
- longer-term: better pod placement policies to avoid AZ correlated restarts.

——
Informal wrap: felt like a spaghetti of small things this morning — kernel + heuristic + infra all nudging each other. Good first cut experiments; main priority is to reduce blast radius (pin) and get clear isolation tests.
